title: Keyboard Manager shortcut remapping is unstable and randomly invalid
author: curtin18
summary: Keyboard Manager remaps intermittently stop, but reports disagree on whether the failure is global, app-specific, migration-related, or recovered by restarting PowerToys versus the target application.
next_action: Request one bounded lifecycle matrix for global versus app-specific remaps.

confidence.rationale: The current public evidence does not yet select one reliable implementation path.

judgment.rationale: The thread combines at least three behaviors—global remaps stopping, app-specific remaps recovering when the target app restarts, and migrated/chord settings recovering after toggle. Existing diagnostic archives contain no Keyboard Manager error, so the exact failing lifecycle must be separated.
evidence: The original report says restarting the target application restores the mapping.
Another reporter sees failures across Microsoft 365 apps that can paste clipboard content instead.
A later reporter says remaps fail after system restart until the mapping is toggled off/on and chords are disabled.
The latest triage comment asks whether only application shortcuts are affected and which process restart repairs the failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Request one bounded lifecycle matrix for global versus app-specific remaps.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current public evidence does not yet justify a PowerToys fix plan for this artifact.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager remaps intermittently stop, but reports disagree on whether the failure is global, app-specific, migration-related, or recovered by restarting PowerToys versus the target application.
known_information: PowerToys 0.98.1 and the new editor are represented.
Multiple bug report archives are attached.
The supplied logs show no Keyboard Manager warning or error.
Issue #45953 was closed as a duplicate of this more detailed thread.
inferences: App-specific process identity changes and stale loaded mapping state are competing hypotheses.
A single exact before/after matrix is more useful than another generic diagnostic package.
issue_context.analysis: The current evidence cannot support one safe fix because the reported recovery actions imply different owners. The reporter can provide the smallest discriminating matrix without additional tooling.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full live body, all comments, diagnostic references, and duplicate #45953.
Verified #45953 was closed in favor of this issue, so this remains the canonical thread.

information_gaps.information: Whether the failure affects global remaps, app-specific remaps, or both, and whether restarting the target app, restarting PowerToys, or toggling the mapping restores each case.
information_gaps.why_needed: These outcomes distinguish target-process matching from stale Keyboard Manager hook/configuration state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: When the failure next occurs, test one global and one app-specific remap before changing anything, then try the three recovery actions one at a time and report the result.

information_gaps.information: One exact remap tuple and target application that fails reliably enough to repeat.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current examples span different applications and migrated settings, preventing a focused regression test.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the trigger, output, app scope/executable name, whether chords are enabled, and the shortest sequence from restart to failure.

actions.label: Confirm remap scope and recovery path
actions.note: Draft only; no comment or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body:
Thanks for the attached reports and the observations about application restart and mapping toggles. The remaining ambiguity is whether this is target-process matching or stale Keyboard Manager state.

**Needed**
1. When it next fails, please test one global and one app-specific remap, then report separately whether restarting the target app, restarting PowerToys, or toggling that mapping restores each one.
2. Please provide one exact failing tuple: trigger, output, app scope/executable name, chord setting, and the shortest sequence from restart to failure.

This matrix will select the correct lifecycle path to investigate without repeating the diagnostics already attached.
